meta.question: Which combination of additives A and B gives the highest score?
meta.context: Synthetic demo data, not experimental results: six cycles of 15 formulations, repeats, a second instrument, an impedance cell, an oven and a handful of side questions.

Q.title: Which additives A and B give the highest score?
Q.why: Screen formulations in cycles of 15 runs, and let each cycle choose where the next one looks.

evidence.noData: The question itself: no numbers of its own.

C1.title: Cycle 1: 15 formulations over the whole range
C1.why: Start without assumptions: spread the first 15 runs over A and B from 0 to 5 wt%.

result.text: Median score 0.15, but one run stood out: 0.89 at A 2.14, B 1.47 wt%.

C1.note: Most of the range scores low; the one good run is the lead to follow.

links.note: the 0.89 run at A 2.14 wt% was the first sign of the good region

X1.title: High additive B (above 3.5 wt%)
X1.why: B is cheap: if more of it helped, the formulation would cost less.
X1.reason: None of the 3 runs with B above 3.5 wt% in cycles 1 and 2 scored above 0.06.

result.text: 3 runs with B above 3.5 wt%, best score 0.06.

X1.population: Cycles 1 and 2, runs with B above 3.5 wt%

links.note: high B scored low in cycle 1; cycle 5 found the same for B above 2

X3.title: Add a third additive C
X3.why: A third additive could open a direction that A and B alone do not have.
X3.reason: The supplier quoted five times the price of B; a formulation that expensive would not be used, whatever it scores.

result.text: No runs were made; decided from the price list.

evidence.noData: Decided from the supplier price list; no runs were made.

L1.title: Reading: the reported optimum of A is near 2.4 wt%
L1.why: Before spending a cycle, see what is known about A in similar systems.

result.text: One review puts the optimum of A at about 2.4 wt%, in a cell of another size.

L1.note: It agrees with cycle 1 (the 0.89 run at A 2.14), but the cell differs, so it is a hint, not a result.

source.title: Review of additive A in this kind of cell (reading notes)

mark.note: One paper, a different cell size.

X9.title: High B, but with little A
X9.why: High B might work where A does not get in its way.
X9.reason: Every run with B above 2.5 and A below 1.8 wt% scored 0.06 or less.

result.text: 2 runs of cycles 1 and 2, best 0.06.

X9.population: Cycles 1 and 2, B above 2.5 and A below 1.8 wt%

C2.title: Cycle 2: the model's suggestions
C2.why: Let the model pick 15 formulations from cycle 1.
C2.reason: The best run reached only 0.74; the cycle mixed a search of the edges with runs near the lead.

result.text: Median 0.31, best 0.74: higher than cycle 1 overall, lower at the top.

C2.note: Read at first as "the model got worse"; see the correction R1.

C3.title: Cycle 3: concentrate on A 1.9–3.31 wt%
C3.why: Cycles 1 and 2 point to the middle of the A range; stop exploring the edges.

result.text: 14 of 15 runs scored 0.7 or more; median 0.85, best 0.96 at A 2.51, B 1.54 wt%.

C3.note: The search has found the high-scoring region (Figure 1 of the report).

milestone.reason: From here the question is where exactly in this region, not where.

R1.title: Cycle 2 was exploring the edges on purpose
R1.why: The low top score of cycle 2 looked like a worse model. The runs say otherwise.

result.text: 6 of 15 runs were at A below 1 or above 3 wt%; the 4 runs between 2 and 3 wt% had a median of 0.50.

R1.note: The model was not worse; it spent half the cycle checking the edges.
R1.population: Cycle 2, all 15 runs, split by A

X2.title: Low additive A (below 1 wt%)
X2.why: A little A might be enough.
X2.reason: The 5 runs with A below 1 wt% in cycles 1 and 2 scored 0.15 at best.

result.text: 5 runs, best score 0.15.

X2.population: Cycles 1 and 2, runs with A below 1 wt%

U1.title: Ask the supplier: is B the same batch in every run?
U1.why: If B changed between runs, part of the spread in cycle 2 would not come from the formulation.

result.text: The same batch (number 7) was used in cycles 1 and 2.

evidence.noData: An email from the supplier; it is not in the folder.

X4.title: Repeat the best cycle-2 run at 60 °C
X4.why: A warmer cell might raise the score of the best formulation of cycle 2.
X4.reason: The oven reached only about 45 °C in two of the three runs, so 60 °C was never tested.

result.text: Set 60 °C, measured 44.8, 45.6 and 60.1 °C; scores 0.61, 0.58 and 0.84.

mark.note: The oven was not checked before the runs.

files.note: set and measured temperature of each run

X8.title: Very high A (above 3.4 wt%)
X8.why: Cycle 1 hinted that more A might keep helping.
X8.reason: Every run above 3.4 wt% of A scored under 0.52.

result.text: 8 runs with A above 3.4 wt%, best score 0.52.

X8.population: Cycles 1 and 2, runs with A above 3.4 wt%

M1.title: Why did the model pick the edges? Its kernel has no A–B interaction
M1.why: Cycle 2 spent 6 of 15 runs at the edges of A; the model must have had a reason.

result.text: The model scored the edges as uncertain, so it explored them: it was meant to. With no interaction term it also missed that A and B peak together.

evidence.noData: Read from the model settings; the settings file is not in the folder.

X10.title: Low A, but cured twice as long
X10.why: Longer curing might make up for little A.
X10.reason: Twice the curing time would halve what the line can make; not worth testing.

result.text: Not run: decided from the production schedule.

M4.title: Train a neural network on the runs instead
M4.why: A network could learn the interaction without being told.
M4.reason: Even after cycle 5 there are only 75 runs, too few for a network; it would fit the noise.

result.text: Not trained: dropped after counting the runs.

L2.title: A second paper puts the optimum of A at 3.1 wt%
L2.why: One paper is a hint; look for a second.
L2.reason: The two papers disagree, and neither gives its raw data.

result.text: Optimum of A: 2.4 wt% in the first paper, 3.1 wt% in the second.

AUD.title: Recompute the top five from the raw files
AUD.why: Before writing it up, check that the table of the best runs comes out of the raw files unchanged.

result.text: Rerunning combine_cycles.py gives the same table; the top five are runs #40, #43, #39, #36, #44.

M5.title: Fit the log of the score: a bell-shaped peak becomes a quadratic
M5.why: If the peak is bell-shaped, its logarithm is a quadratic with an A–B term, which a small fit can find.

result.text: On cycles 1 and 2 alone (28 runs), the fit already put the top at A 2.70, B 1.49 wt%.

M5.note: Nobody used it then: cycle 3 followed the best runs instead.

mark.note: The idea M3 came back to.

M5.population: Cycles 1 and 2, runs scoring 0.05 or more

links.note: the same fit, three weeks earlier

L3.title: The two papers do not use the same score
L3.why: Before choosing between them, check that they measure the same thing.

result.text: The second paper scores after 50 cycles, the first after 5: the optimum moves with the score, not between the papers.

evidence.noData: Reading notes only; the methods sections of the two papers.

U3.title: Why is run #34 of cycle 3 so low?
U3.why: One run of cycle 3 fell far below the others.

result.text: Run #34 is at A 3.31, B 1.33 wt%, the farthest from the middle of the region; it scored 0.68. Not an error, the edge of the region.

X5.title: Follow the impedance drift as a second score
X5.why: The best runs of cycle 3 may differ in how stable they are, which the score alone does not show.
X5.reason: The impedance cell was not calibrated, so a drift cannot be told from noise. The idea was not really tested.

result.text: A drift of about 12 % over five cycles was seen, but it cannot be trusted.

X5.population: The five best runs of cycle 3

mark.note: Worth repeating once the cell is calibrated.

evidence.noData: Measured on the bench; the calibration log was not kept.

checks.population: The five best runs of cycle 3
checks.note: The measurement file was overwritten; only the number in the notes is left.

B1.title: Cycles 3 and 4 used different batches of B: compare them
B1.why: Batch 8 in cycle 3, batch 9 in cycle 4: if the batch mattered, near-identical formulations would score differently.
B1.reason: Pairs of near-identical formulations score the same with either batch: the batch is not what moves the score.

result.text: 14 pairs within 0.25 wt% in A and B; batch 9 minus batch 8: -0.008 on average.

B1.population: Cycles 3 and 4, pairs of near-identical formulations

links.note: the batch did not make cycle 4

R2.title: Repeat at 60 °C with the calibrated oven
R2.why: X4 failed because of the oven, not because of the idea; the idea deserves a fair test.

result.text: Measured 59.8 to 60.2 °C; scores 0.86, 0.88 and 0.85.

R2.note: 60 °C does not hurt and does not help: the median is the same as at room temperature (cycle 3, 0.85). Temperature is not a lever.
R2.population: Three repeats of the same formulation as in X4

milestone.reason: The oven, not the temperature, ruined X4.

files.note: set and measured temperature of each run

C4.title: Cycle 4: confirm the region (A 1.97–2.88 wt%)
C4.why: Repeat inside the region with new formulations, to see whether the scores hold.

result.text: All 15 runs scored 0.7 or more; median 0.87, best 0.96 at A 2.64, B 1.37 wt%.

milestone.reason: The best formulation so far: A 2.64, B 1.37 wt%, score 0.962.

C4.note: The high-scoring region holds with new formulations.

O1.title: Read the oven log of a long day
O1.why: R2 fixed the start of the bake; nobody had looked at the end of a long day.

result.text: Steady for two hours, then 3.3 °C lower by the fourth hour.

O1.population: One day of the oven, every 20 minutes

links.note: the lowest run of cycle 6 was baked at the end of the day

B2.title: Batch 9 looked darker: measure its purity
B2.why: A colour change could mean an impurity that the scores do not show yet.
B2.reason: The purity meter was out of order that week; the question is open, not answered.

evidence.noData: No measurement: the meter was broken.

O2.title: Bake in batches of two hours at most
O2.why: Stay where the oven is steady.

B3.title: Send a sample of batch 9 to the supplier

AUD2.title: Recompute the summary of all cycles from the raw files
AUD2.why: The numbers of the earlier cycles went into slides and texts by hand. Recompute them once, from the raw files.

result.text: The summary of six cycles comes out of the raw files; one number in an earlier slide does not match.

files.note: the scores of every cycle; the red line is the median

checks.claim: Cycle 2: runs at A below 1 or above 3 wt%

checks.note: The slide rounded the best run up; the raw file gives 0.962.

P2.title: Recalibrate the impedance cell, then repeat
P2.why: A calibrated cell would tell whether the drift is real.

result.text: Calibrated: the five best runs of cycle 3 still drift by 10.2 % on average over five cycles.

P2.reason: The drift is real, but it could come from the cell or from the room.
P2.population: The five best runs of cycle 3

X7.title: Pick the runs of cycle 6 by hand, on a grid
X7.why: A grid around the best run would be easy to explain.
X7.reason: Replaced by cycle 6, which takes the model's suggestions on a grid, so the choice of runs is not biased by hand.

I1.title: Does the drift follow the room temperature?
I1.why: The room warmed during the week of the measurements.

result.text: Step by step, the change of impedance follows the change of temperature (correlation 0.67, 20 steps).

I1.note: A correlation of 1 means they rise and fall together; 0, no relation. It shows they move together, not that one causes the other.
I1.population: The five best runs of cycle 3, cycles 1 to 5

U2.title: Run the best formulation on the second instrument
U2.why: Check that the score does not depend on the instrument.

result.text: The best run of cycle 4: 0.962 on instrument 1, 0.903 on instrument 2.

I4.title: Ask the lab: is the room air-conditioned at night?
I4.why: A warmer room every day would explain the trend.

result.text: No: the air conditioning is off from Friday to Monday.

C5.title: Cycle 5: larger B inside the good A range (B 1.8–3.4 wt%)
C5.why: The next steps of the report: look for higher scores at larger B inside the good A range.
C5.reason: The score falls as B grows: the five runs with the smallest B had a median of 0.69, the five with the largest B only 0.16.

result.text: Median 0.48, best 0.84 at B 1.82 wt%; 2 of 15 runs scored 0.7 or more.

files.note: every run of the search in the A-B plane, coloured by score

I2.title: Take the temperature out of the drift
I2.why: If temperature explains the drift, what is left is the drift of the cell.
I2.reason: What is left, about 0.3 %, is the size of the noise of the cell: there may be no drift at all, or a small one.

result.text: Drift over five cycles: 10.2 % measured, 0.3 % after taking out the temperature.

I2.population: The five best runs of cycle 3

V1.title: Measure the eight best runs on both instruments
V1.why: One sample cannot tell an offset from noise.

result.text: Instrument 2 reads 0.054 lower on average, and all eight still score high there; their order is partly shuffled (rank correlation 0.64).

V1.note: A rank correlation of 1 would be the same order; 0, no relation. Runs that differ by less than the noise change places, as T1 found.
V1.population: The eight best runs of cycles 3 and 4

links.note: the region holds on the other instrument
the order of the best runs is noise

I3.title: Measure in the climate chamber
I3.why: At a fixed temperature, any drift left is the cell.

evidence.noData: Planned: the chamber is booked for June.

R3.title: Five runs of cycle 2 were measured on instrument 2
R3.why: The instrument log shows that cycle 2 used both instruments; its scores mix the two.

result.text: Runs #16, #21, #23, #27, #29 were on instrument 2: median 0.17, or 0.22 with the offset taken out. The median of all 15 runs stays 0.31: the conclusion of cycle 2 holds.

links.note: scores of five runs were from instrument 2

checks.population: Cycle 2, five runs shifted by the offset

T1.title: Repeat the best run of cycle 4 six times
T1.why: Before going further from single best runs, know how much one formulation scatters by itself.

result.text: Six repeats: 0.87 to 0.92, standard deviation 0.017. The five best runs of cycles 3 and 4 lie within 0.02 of each other.

T1.note: The best run of cycle 4 scored 0.96; its six repeats average 0.90, so part of that score was luck. The noise of one run is as large as the differences between the best runs: ranking single runs ranks noise.
T1.population: One formulation (A 2.64, B 1.37 wt%), six repeats

milestone.reason: From the highest single run to the best region: the search changes its goal.

mark.note: Should have been done after cycle 3.

files.note: six repeats of the best run of cycle 4

T2.title: How many of the best runs can be told apart?
T2.why: With the spread of T1, count the runs that are as good as the best within the noise.

result.text: 7 runs of cycles 3 and 4 are within two standard deviations (0.035) of the best one.

V2.title: Calibrate instrument 2 against the reference sample
V2.why: An offset measured on eight runs is a correction, not a calibration.

M3.title: Rank by a surface fitted to all runs, not by single runs
M3.why: Every run carries information about the region, not only the best ones; a surface averages the noise out.

result.text: The log of the score fitted with a quadratic surface (73 runs; it explains 90 % of the variation in log scale): top at A 2.66, B 1.50 wt%.

M3.note: The best single run of cycle 4 (A 2.64, B 1.37) sits close to the top, but not on it.
M3.population: Cycles 1 to 5, runs scoring 0.05 or more

links.note: the best run of cycle 4 is near the top, not the top

R4.title: The top five of the audit are equals, not a ranking
R4.why: The audit listed the top five runs in order; T1 shows that order is within the noise.

result.text: The five runs differ by 0.02 at most, less than two standard deviations of one run (0.035).

R4.population: The five best runs of cycles 3 and 4

links.note: the order of the top five is noise

T3.title: Repeat each of the top five three times
T3.why: Repeats would show whether any of the five is really better.

C6.title: Cycle 6: a fine grid between the best run and the top of the surface
C6.why: The surface puts the top at A 2.66, B 1.50 wt%, the best run of cycle 4 at A 2.64, B 1.37: cover both with a fine grid.

result.text: 8 of 15 runs measured: best 0.97 so far, the lowest 0.89.

C6.population: Cycle 6, the 8 runs measured so far

checks.note: Two runs were added after the number was written.

A3.title: Fit the surface again without each cycle
A3.why: A top that moves a lot when one cycle is left out would not be worth a cycle of runs.

result.text: Leaving out one cycle at a time, the top stays between A 2.57 and 2.67, B 1.34 and 1.53 wt%.

P3.title: Repeat the best formulation 15 times
P3.why: To know the spread of the best formulation itself.

P4.title: Scale the best formulation up to a 10× batch
P4.why: The question that follows from the result.

K1.title: Use A 2.6, B 1.4 wt% for the next stage
K1.why: What the search is meant to deliver.

P5.title: Run the top of the surface on the second instrument
P5.why: The next stage uses the second instrument.

P6.title: Write the method: how the cycles chose their runs
P6.why: The turn from single runs to the surface has to be explained to the next team.

P7.title: Check batch 10 of B before the next stage
P7.why: Batches 8 and 9 behaved the same; a new batch should be checked once, not assumed.

k-01.after: The impedance cell was not calibrated, so a drift cannot be told from noise. The idea was not really tested.

k-03.after: The summary of six cycles comes out of the raw files; one number in an earlier slide does not match.

k-04.after: Replaced by cycle 6, which takes the model's suggestions on a grid, so the choice of runs is not biased by hand.

k-09.after: Even after cycle 5 there are only 75 runs, too few for a network; it would fit the noise.

k-10.after: What is left, about 0.3 %, is the size of the noise of the cell: there may be no drift at all, or a small one.

k-13.after: The log of the score fitted with a quadratic surface (73 runs; it explains 90 % of the variation in log scale): top at A 2.66, B 1.50 wt%.

after.reason: From the highest single run to the best region: the search changes its goal.
